name: Golden labels (truth reconstruction)
question: What are the true values behind the 20% mask?
setup: 24,634 masked targets in 15,964 prompts across 13 data types, rebuilt from Sid Sijbrandij's public bucket (s3://sid-sijbrandij-osteosarc-dataset) and validated against training values.
where: GitHub biohack: 02_golden_labels/ (gold itself is not committed); ~/osteo-golden

name: Glimmer-30B zero-shot
question: How well does an untrained 30B model fill in missing values from the entity's other values?
setup: Muse-Glimmer-30B, greedy, one prompt per entity listing its observed values of that type and the items to predict; 54 truncated prompts re-run with a larger budget.

name: Glimmer LoRA sid_full
question: Does supervised fine-tuning on the patient's own visible data help?
setup: LoRA r32 α64 on all 11,824 training rows, lr 1e-4 cosine, max length 6,144, completion-only loss. Stopped at step 739 of 1,478 (half an epoch, learning rate still mid-schedule).

name: Muse Spark 1.3 and 1.2 zero-shot
question: Does a larger hosted model know more biology than Glimmer, without fine-tuning?
setup: Same 15,964 prompts via the Meta Model API (contributor tier), temperature 0, reasoning effort low, cut-offs retried with 16k tokens. Unanswered prompts count as unanswered.

name: Context-free Glimmer (own type stripped)
question: If an entity has no observed values of a data type at all, can the model still predict it?
setup: Prompts for flow, bulk RNA, TCR and Xenium with every observed value of that type removed. Eval prompts never carry other data types, so this is the model's prior alone.
compute: NVIDIA-hosted meta/muse-glimmer-30b (free tier, ~2 min per request)

name: Leave-one-data-type-out LoRA (LOMO)
status: flow, RNA, TCR, all-data done; Xenium eval running
question: How much of the fine-tune gain on a data type survives when that type is removed from training, and what does removing it do to the others?
setup: Same recipe as sid_full, fixed 740-step schedule run to completion (5,920 rows seen), one type's training rows removed; then evaluated on all 15,964 prompts. lomo740_all is the matched all-data reference.

name: Classical imputation (22 methods)
question: How far do simple data-only methods get, with no prior knowledge?
setup: Feature/entity means and medians, additive effects, entity- and feature-kNN (k 5–50), biased ALS (rank 2/8/32, λ 1/10) and a gradient-boosted stack, in asinh space, on visible values only. Per-type pick chosen on a 10% split of visible values, never on eval targets.

name: Cross-data-type prediction
question: Which data types carry information about which others?
setup: Gene link: each other type's level of the same gene (mean asinh + detection rate) added as features to the GBM stack, with drop-one and source-alone ablations; validation holds out whole features to mimic never-observed targets. Date link: cross-modal kNN between samples drawn within 21 days.

name: ET-SoC-1 accelerator run
question: Can the kNN similarity step run on the Esperanto ET-SoC-1 card?
setup: CITE-seq entity-kNN similarity S = A·Aᵀ (A = 8,656 × 400, 60 GFLOP) on aifoundry3 card 0: 373 ms per launch, 160 GFLOP/s, max abs error 4.2e-7; kNN predictions identical to CPU.

name: Classical hold-out settings (S1/S2/S3)
question: Can classical methods predict a data type with none of it anywhere, with only other samples of it, or with only the sample's own values?
setup: All 12 numeric types. S1 type absent: predict 0, other types' gene level, or a GBM trained on other types. S2 new sample: leave-sample-out feature mean/median, carry-forward from the previous draw, nearest draw, and a GBM with gene links. S3 type unseen in training: the sample's own mean/median, or a GBM trained on every other type. Same targets and scorer as all runs; random mask, not a time split.
